sources.title: Frantz Grenet, Kidarites, Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.note: Direct article read. Opening and historical narrative distinguish disputed initial dates, loss of Tokharistan in 467 and a residual Gandharan kingdom, possibly in Swat, sending embassies until 477. This does not establish a Kushan state throughout the imported 500-600 span.

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Iranica, Kushanshahs i. History
sources.note: Direct article read, final discussion of successor coin issues and Kidarite use of Kushanshah. The survival of royal names and titles is distinguished from uninterrupted dynastic government.

sources.title: Hans Bakker, A Buddhist Foundation in Śārdīysa (2018)
sources.note: Original research article, Indo-Iranian Journal 61, pp. 1-19. Read indexed original article text mirrored at https://www.scribd.com/document/791162747/15728536-06101001; direct mirror extraction failed. Exact query: "A Buddhist Foundation in Śārdīysa" "wife". Pp. 4-5 provide contents and alternative 492/93 or 495/96 dating; abstract and pp. 14-16 argue Punjab/Kashmir provenance instead of Bactria. Proposed location is not a secure excavation findspot.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Buddhism along the Silk Road: 5th-8th Century (2012)
sources.note: Direct indexed museum exhibition text read. Trade through Khyber and Karakoram passes financed images in Gandhara and Swat; cross-regional artistic connections continued in the sixth century. Older generalized Hunnic/Hephthalite political terminology is not adopted as a precise dynasty identification.

sources.title: British Museum, Kidarite silver coin from Hadda Stupa 10, 1894,0506.135
sources.note: Direct museum object record: circa fourth-fifth century, silver, 27 mm, 3.67 g, Afghanistan mint attribution. Curator identified the coin through Masson manuscript drawing as from Tope Kelan/Hadda Stupa 10, excavated in 1834. Explicit earlier background; not an exact sixth-century coin or proof of the atlas border.

sources.title: UNESCO, Buddhist Ruins of Takht-i-Bahi and Sahr-i-Bahlol
sources.note: Direct Outstanding Universal Value, Brief Synthesis: monastery founded early first century, continuous use until seventh; stone/mortar construction, meditation cells, conference hall, covered stepped passageways. Whole-complex surviving plan is not assigned exclusively to the sixth century. Modern drainage problems are not used as evidence of ancient sanitation.

sources.title: Dániel Balogh, ed., Hunnic Peoples in Central and South Asia (2020)
sources.note: Original scholarly sourcebook by Barkhuis read directly through full text mirror. I.053/C, printed pp. 68-69: Qielanji 5, Song Yun regional observations, vegetarian king, music, grains/fruits and offerings; X.030, printed pp. 322-325: Melzer translation of donor list, father Opanda, women, teacher and prayer for health. Entire book URL has one budget. Late account of Kashmir raw vegetables may reuse Han text and is deliberately omitted.

sources.title: DHARMA, Schøyen Copper Scroll Inscription, INSSiddham00102
sources.note: Direct critical Sanskrit edition by Dániel Balogh, based on Gudrun Melzer and Lore Sander. B19 reads sārdhaṁ pitrā Opandena with no restoration in these words; translated by Melzer in Balogh 2020, X.030, p. 324, donor 2. Modern Devanagari display is editorial transcription, not original Brahmi glyphs. B19-22 donor family/women, B21 teacher; A3ff sutra and B15-16 philosophical verse; B29-30 prayer for health. Some surrounding letters and names are damaged.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Standing Buddha with Radiate Combined Halo
sources.note: Direct indexed museum record, accession 1981.188a, b, circa late sixth century, brass, height 33.7 cm. Current record used rather than older acquisition catalogue calling the alloy bronze and measuring 33.6 cm. Gandharan/Gupta stylistic blend and portability are museum interpretations; maker and findspot are not supplied.

sources.title: Kurt Behrendt, The Art of Gandhara in the Metropolitan Museum of Art (2007)
sources.note: Original museum monograph, printed p. 89, Decline of Buddhism in Greater Gandhara, read in extensive indexed original PDF text. Reproducible query: "The Art of Gandhara" "continued" "Hun". Direct web PDF opening failed. Discusses fewer post-500 coins, reduced patronage, continuing occupation/limited construction and late coins in Dharmarajika/Manikyala relic deposits. Rejects a uniform destruction interpretation.

proposedOverrides.name: Kushan Principalities
proposedOverrides.summary: An uncertain atlas label for northwestern regions after the earlier Kushan and Kidarite powers.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Retain exact indexed label and 500-600 map coverage, with prominent public uncertainty. Regional post-Kushan material is explicitly distinguished from a securely attested unified Kushan polity. Existing kushan-empire is a different earlier record and is not shared. No Kidara/Kidarite indexed alias exists. No geometry or chronology edits proposed.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: Alchon-period Sanskrit copper scroll is a regional comparative witness around 500, not a Kushan royal document. Original Brahmi-family script displayed only in modern Devanagari transcription; provenance and date conversion remain debated.
